content: (I'd also like to thank @Heather Macbeth for telling me about this tactic and enthusing about it. Of course this implementation is not at all her fault. And, of course, thanks to John Harrison for writing the original tactic in HOL Light; this implementation slavishly copies his decisions wherever possible.)
This is very exciting! IIRC, one of the complications Harrison talks about in his paper comes from rounding/rationally approximating the results from the SDP solver. How is your tool handling this?

Slavishly copying Harrison's decisions. :-) Our rounding regime (try small ints first, then some powers of two) is lifted from the HOL Light implementation.

(Actually, before your message, it was a slight variation of the rounding regime (more small ints, some 3*2^k, and fewer powers of two. But in checking, none of those variants are actually justified by the current test suite, so I've reverted to exactly copying Harrison.)

I'm actually thinking about putting in an intermediate library between csdp-ffi and sos that handles the rounding regime as a reusable layer.

This is great! I see that this tactic cannot prove the nonnegativity of the Motzkin polynomial. Can Harrison's tactic do it? I was thinking about writing a tactic in Lean that can handle it as well (using SDP too).

Vasilii Nesterov said:

This is great! I see that this tactic cannot prove the nonnegativity of the Motzkin polynomial. Can Harrison's tactic do it? I was thinking about writing a tactic in Lean that can handle it as well (using SDP too).

We can do it now, see https://github.com/leanprover/sos/blob/dfc5720/SOSTest/Showcase.lean#L33-L41:

example (x y : ℝ) :
    0 ≤ x^4*y^2 + x^2*y^4 + 1 - 3*x^2*y^2 := by
  sos (config := { maxRefutationPower := 1 })
